# Vulnerabilities that govulncheck can trace from helmtide's own code into a
# vulnerable symbol, and that we accept for now. .github/scripts/govulncheck.sh
# fails the build on anything reachable that is not listed here, so this file is
# the whole difference between a gate and a `|| true`.
#
# One id per line; everything after # is a comment. Every entry is somebody
# saying "I looked at this and it cannot be fixed from here yet", so each one
# records why it is in and what takes it out. Nothing is listed because it was
# noisy, and nothing is listed that has a fixed version we could move to.
#
# Standard library advisories do not belong here. The scan runs on the newest
# stable toolchain, so a stdlib finding means Go has not shipped the patch yet;
# if one is reported as NEW, wait for the patch release or pin a fixed one --
# do not add it below. (Scanning with the 1.25.8 from go.mod instead would list
# 14 stdlib advisories Go fixed in 1.25.9 - 1.25.12. That is the reason the job
# does not use go-version-file.)
#
# Last reviewed: 2026-08-04, govulncheck v1.6.0, Go 1.26.5, vuln db 2026-07-27.
# Reachable then: exactly the four below.

# The golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package is unmaintained and unsafe by design.
# The advisory covers every version that has ever existed and has no fixed one,
# so there is nothing to upgrade to. We do not import it: helm does, to check
# chart provenance (LocateChart) and signed repository indexes
# (DownloadIndexFile). It goes away when helm stops using x/crypto/openpgp.
GO-2026-5932

# Three containerd CRI checkpoint/restore holes: symlink following in the log
# path (CVE-2026-53489), image tag poisoning on checkpoint import
# (CVE-2026-50195) and CDI annotation smuggling on restore (CVE-2026-53492).
#
# All three are fixed only in the github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 module
# (2.1.9, 2.2.5); for the v1 module every advisory is "introduced at 0" with no
# fix event, i.e. the 1.x line is not getting one. We are on v1.7.33 as an
# indirect dependency of helm.sh/helm/v3/pkg/registry, so it moves when helm
# moves to containerd v2, and not before.
#
# The advisories name no vulnerable packages for the v1 module, which is why
# every trace govulncheck offers is package initialisation (release.init ->
# registry.init -> images.init and friends) rather than a call into the CRI
# checkpoint code. helmtide has no way to reach that code: it uses containerd's
# remotes/images packages to pull charts from an OCI registry and never speaks
# to a containerd daemon, let alone checkpoints a container.
GO-2026-5622
GO-2026-5338
GO-2026-5064
